caption: The drawing depicts a headdress composed of a band and a collection of upright feathers. The feathers, drawn with shades of gray, brown, and hints of yellow, are arranged along the top edge of the headdress and fan outwards. The band at the base is a scalloped strip, predominantly red with green and black outlining along the curves, and decorated with simple patterns in light green and white. The band also shows a faint blue section at the base. Surrounding the drawing are various handwritten notations identifying the objects and providing details: "HEAD DRESS - Malecite Tribe," noting the use of "FEATHERS - CLOTH, BEAD & METAL DECORATION," and indicating the width as "1 foot – 8 inches wide." Additional writing at the top and bottom edges includes labels such as "E. WOODLAND HALL," the case number, initials, and a date of "Oct 8th, 1935" attributed to "Mary Brenner." The background is plain and beige, with the drawing and text done in colored pencil and pencil.
title: Head Dress
